messages.content: I need to put together a Chicago trip for a university-press rights conference, Thursday, March 26 through Sunday, March 29. I’ll be leaving from Denver. Can you help me compare flights and hotels as complete combinations rather than separate lists?

Yes. What time does your Thursday office commitment end, when is the exhibitor briefing, and where is the conference being held? I’ll also need the end time of the last Sunday session before I narrow the return flights.

My office commitment should finish at 10:30 Thursday morning, and I can head straight to DEN from campus. The exhibitor briefing starts at 6:00 p.m. at the Palmer House, with check-in requested by 5:30. The final session Sunday ends at 2:15 p.m. Everything is on Central Time.

That makes a departure before about noon difficult once airport travel and security are included. For a reasonable arrival margin, I’ll look at nonstop flights leaving DEN roughly noon to 1:30 p.m. and landing by 4:30 p.m. On Sunday, leaving the hotel around 2:30 after the session suggests an ORD departure no earlier than about 5:15 p.m., or a Midway departure after about 4:45. Is the trip for one traveler, and do you need a room for all three nights?

One traveler, one room, checking in Thursday and out Sunday. Those flight windows sound right. I don’t need to stay in the Palmer House itself, but I don’t want a hotel that turns the briefing into a complicated cross-town trip.

Understood. I found three workable pairings based on the current schedules and displayed rates. Prices are snapshots and can change before purchase.

Option A: United nonstop DEN–ORD, 12:05–3:28 p.m. Thursday; return ORD–DEN, 6:10–7:52 p.m. Sunday. Palmer House room for three nights, about $846 including taxes. Estimated combined total: $1,214. You would already be at the venue, and the Thursday flight leaves about 90 minutes from landing to the requested check-in time.

Option B: Southwest nonstop DEN–MDW, 12:35–3:52 p.m.; return MDW–DEN, 5:35–7:15 p.m. Sunday. Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown South Loop, about $612 including taxes. Estimated combined total: $934. The hotel is roughly a 20-minute walk or a short ride from Palmer House. Thursday arrival leaves less buffer than A, but Midway is closer to the Loop.

Option C: United nonstop DEN–ORD, 1:00–4:20 p.m.; return ORD–DEN, 7:05–8:47 p.m. Sunday. Club Quarters Central Loop, about $681 including taxes. Estimated combined total: $1,019. The hotel is around a 7-minute walk from Palmer House, but the outbound timing is tight enough that a modest delay could make the briefing check-in stressful.
Option C is too tight on Thursday. Between A and B, can you account for getting from each airport to the hotel? The listed total makes B look better, but I want to understand the actual timing.

For Option A, landing at ORD at 3:28 gives you 2 hours 2 minutes until requested check-in. Allowing 15–25 minutes to reach the curb and 35–60 minutes by taxi or rideshare in Thursday traffic, you would likely reach Palmer House around 4:20–4:55. The Blue Line is more predictable but requires a transfer or a walk with luggage; a realistic hotel arrival would be around 4:45–5:05.

For Option B, landing at MDW at 3:52 leaves 1 hour 38 minutes. A taxi or rideshare to the South Loop hotel generally takes 25–45 minutes, followed by the trip to Palmer House. Even with a quick check-in, arrival at the briefing venue would likely fall around 5:05–5:30. Going directly from Midway to Palmer House first would improve that to roughly 4:45–5:15, with hotel check-in after the briefing.

So B remains viable if you go straight to the conference venue. A gives the cleaner sequence and more protection against normal ground delays.
Please drop C. Is there another hotel near Palmer House that brings the United combination below the cost of staying at the conference hotel?

Two nearby alternatives fit that request. With the same United flights as Option A, the Central Loop Hotel is displaying about $654 including taxes for three nights, putting the combined estimate near $1,022. It is about a 6-minute walk from Palmer House. The Silversmith Hotel is about a 3-minute walk and is displaying roughly $732 including taxes, for a combined estimate near $1,100.

The Central Loop pairing saves about $192 against staying at Palmer House while preserving the stronger flight schedule. The Silversmith saves about $114 and has the shortest walk, but its room rate is closer to the conference hotel’s.
How does the Central Loop room compare with the Hilton Garden Inn room? I’ll need somewhere to work between appointments on Friday, but I’m not looking for anything elaborate.

The standard Central Loop room is compact and includes a desk, Wi-Fi, and an on-site club-style lounge or shared work area, depending on the room listing. The Hilton Garden Inn room is generally larger and also has a desk; the property has a business center and fitness room.

For Friday logistics, Central Loop is the stronger location: you can walk to Palmer House in about 6 minutes and return to the room between appointments without budgeting for a ride. The Hilton Garden Inn gives you more room but is about a mile south, so a quick return between conference meetings is less convenient.

That makes the United plus Central Loop combination the leading one. Before settling on it, check the Sunday timing carefully. I won’t be able to leave the venue before 2:15, and I may need ten minutes afterward to say goodbye to people.

Leaving Palmer House around 2:25 p.m., you could collect a stored bag at Central Loop by about 2:35–2:45. For the 6:10 p.m. ORD flight, a rideshare departing by 2:50 would provide roughly 75–105 minutes for traffic and still put you at the terminal around 4:05–4:35. That leaves about 95 minutes or more before departure.

The Blue Line is another workable route: walk or take a short ride to the nearest convenient station, then allow about 50–65 minutes to the terminal area. The 6:10 departure is viable either way. The later 7:05 flight adds nearly an hour of airport margin but currently costs about $46 more round trip.
Keep the 6:10 return. Could you compare the two remaining complete choices in a small table, including the realistic Thursday plan and the Sunday departure margin?

| Combination | Thursday plan | Hotel access to venue | Sunday plan | Estimated total |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| United via ORD + Central Loop Hotel | DEN 12:05 p.m. → ORD 3:28 p.m.; rideshare to hotel, then 6-minute walk to Palmer House; likely venue arrival 4:30–5:05 p.m. | About 6 minutes on foot | Leave venue about 2:25, collect bag, depart hotel around 2:50 for 6:10 p.m. ORD flight; generally 95+ minutes at airport | $1,022 |
| Southwest via MDW + Hilton Garden Inn South Loop | DEN 12:35 p.m. → MDW 3:52 p.m.; go directly to Palmer House and check into hotel after briefing | About 20 minutes on foot or a short ride | Leave venue about 2:25, collect bag, then depart for 5:35 p.m. MDW flight; workable but with less recovery time | $934 |

The Southwest combination saves about $88. The United combination costs more but allows hotel check-in before the briefing, simplifies movement during the conference, and gives the more comfortable Sunday sequence.
Is the Southwest return really comfortable enough after getting the bag from the South Loop hotel? That part seems rushed.

It is feasible, but I would not describe it as comfortable. From Palmer House at 2:25, reaching the Hilton Garden Inn and retrieving a bag could take until about 2:55. A car to Midway might take 25–45 minutes, producing an airport arrival around 3:20–3:40 for a 5:35 flight. That is adequate under ordinary traffic, but a delayed session, slow hotel stop, or traffic incident would consume the extra margin quickly.

By comparison, the United itinerary gives you another 35 minutes before departure and the bag pickup is only a short walk from the venue. The practical difference is larger than the flight times alone suggest.
All right. Use United with the Central Loop Hotel as the working itinerary. Don’t book anything yet. Please give me the details I should verify when I’m ready to purchase.

Working itinerary:

Thursday, March 26: United nonstop from DEN at 12:05 p.m., arriving ORD at 3:28 p.m. Take a taxi or rideshare to Central Loop Hotel, check in, and walk approximately 6 minutes to Palmer House for the 5:30 p.m. exhibitor check-in and 6:00 briefing.

Hotel: Central Loop Hotel, three nights, Thursday through Sunday, currently about $654 including taxes. Verify that the displayed room has a desk and that the rate’s cancellation deadline remains acceptable before payment. Also confirm whether any destination or facility charge is already included in the quoted total.

Sunday, March 29: After the 2:15 p.m. final session, allow ten minutes at the venue, collect your stored bag from the hotel, and aim to leave for ORD by 2:50 p.m. United nonstop departs at 6:10 p.m. and arrives in Denver at 7:52 p.m.

Current combined estimate: about $1,022 for airfare and room. At purchase, recheck the exact fare rules, baggage allowance, hotel taxes and fees, room cancellation terms, and whether either flight time has changed. Nothing has been booked.
